Learned A.G.A., on the basis of the instructions received, has opposed the prayer for grant of applicant's on bail but he has not disputed the above contention made by the learned counsel for the accused-applicant particularly the fact that the Suyash Agrawal, having similar role, has already been released on bail by this Court.
Learned counsel for the side opposite also could not dispute aforesaid aspect of the case.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the record and also considering the nature of allegations, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties as also that Suyash Agrawal has already been released on bail and without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, prima facie, the contention of the counsel for the applicant appears to be correct, as such, I find it to be a fit case for granting bail.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,

3. The facts relevant are as below:-
Against the present revisionist, an FIR Case Crime No. 698 of 2020 under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 406, 506 IPC was lodged with certain allegations; the accused persons applied for anticipatory bail through Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No. 299 of 2021 wherein a coordinate Bench of this Court passed an interim order dated 13.01.2021 directing the applicants to deposit their passports with the S.S.P./S.P. concerned/Court concerned; consequently they deposited their passports; this anticipatory bail application was admittedly finally decided by order dated 28.01.2021; admittedly the application was dismissed with further direction to the applicants to appear and surrender before the court below and apply for regular Suyash Agarwal And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178909551/
8 bail; thereafter the applicants applied for release of that passport but their application was dismissed by the impugned order on the premise that the passports have been deposited in pursuance of court's interim order dated 13.01.2021; now the revisionists/applicants are before this Court.

sentences.text: 4. It is contended on behalf of the revisionists/applicants that the interim order is no more in existence, as the anticipatory bail application has been finally disposed of with no such direction as regard of deposit of passport; their application for release of passports has been dismissed on an erroneous impression that such an order is still existing.
5. The factual submissions of the revisionists/applicants have not been denied by the other side.
Perusal of the papers show that the prayer for release of the passport has been rejected on the basis of an order which was non-est, at that time.
When the application for anticipatory bail was decided finally, the interim order merged in the same.

6. In view of the above, the impugned order is not sustainable in law, hence it is set-aside with the direction to the court concerned to decide revisionist's application afresh in the light of the provisions of Chapter 34 of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this criminal revision is allowed."

Subsequent to the above order dated 12.05.2023, revisionists again approached court below seeking release of their passports, which prayer has again been negated by court below vide order dated 15.06.2023.
Thus, feeling aggrieved by order dated 15.06.2023 passed by court below, revisionists have now approached this Court by means of present criminal revision.
Learned counsel for revisionists contends that initially anticipatory bail was granted to the revisionists vide orders dated 12.01.2021/13.01.2021.
Therefore, the order of interim/anticipatory bail merged in the final order dated 28.01.2021 as already noted herein-above.
However, the anticipatory bail applications filed by revisionists was rejected by the Court vide order dated 28.01.2021.
Ultimately revisionists were granted regular bail by this Court vide separate orders dated 06.12.2021/04.01.2022.

On the above premise, the learned counsel for revisionists contends that since surrender of the passports by the revisionists before court below is not a condition precedent in the final bail orders dated 06.12.2021/04.01.2022 therefore, by placing reliance upon the directions contained in the order granting ad-interim anticipatory bail to the revisionists, the release of their passports prayed for by the revisionist could not have been denied by court below.
On the above premise, it is thus contended by the learned counsel for revisionists that the order impugned passed by court below on the aforesaid ground is not only illegal but also erroneous.
In view of above, the order impugned cannot be sustained in law and is therefore liable to be set aside by this Court.

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned A.G.A. for State-opposite party 1 and Mr. Sagir Ahmad, the learned senior counsel assisted by Mr. Dharmendra Kumar, the learned counsel representing opposite party 2 have vehemently opposed the present criminal revision.
However, they could not dislodge the legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for revisionists with reference to the record at this stage.

Having heard the learned counsel for revisionists, the learned A.G.A. for State-opposite party 1, the learned senior counsel representing opposite party 2 and upon perusal of record this Court finds that the release application filed by the revisionists seeking release of their passports has been rejected by court below on the ground which is not only illegal but also erroneous.

Admittedly, the anticipatory bail application filed by accused-revisionists in which an ad-interim anticipatory bail was granted to the revisionists was ultimately disposed off finally with a direction to the accused-revisionists to apply for regular bail.
In compliance of this direction, the revisionists approached for bail on the regular side and were ultimately enlarged on bail on the regular side under the orders dated 06.12.2021/04.01.2022.
In the aforesaid orders of this Court, there is no condition that accused-revisionists shall surrender their passports before court below.

Since surrender of the passports before court below was not a condition precedent in the aforementioned regular bail orders therefore, there was no occasion for the revisionists to seek modification of the orders of this Court dated 06.12.2021/04.01.2022.

As already noted above that since surrender of the passports is not a condition precedent in the above orders, referred to above, the view taken to the contrary by court below is not only illegal but also erroneous.

Therefore by exercising power under Section 482 CrPC and Article 227 of the Constitution of India and irrespective of the fact that passports of the revisionists is not a case property and therefore not covered in terms of Section 481 CrPC, the passports of the revisionists are liable to be released.
In view of the discussion made above, the present revision succeeds and is liable to be allowed.
It is, accordingly, allowed.
The order impugned dated dated 15.06.2023, passed by Judicial Magistrate, Court No.3, Varanasi in Case No.8006 of 2021 (State Vs. Suyash Agarwal and others) is set aside.
